title: A guard holds only acts it checks before they take effect; reply guards leave the reconstitution cut
situation: The operator suspected a timing problem in the bottom-line guard. The lead's account from the code: the guard judges the turn's final reply at turn end, after the architect has already taken the turn's acts and, by every sign, after the reply has been shown to the operator; a refusal can only make the agent write a second reply, which the operator also sees, and it cannot undo an act, so about 44 of 344 refusals could not be met truthfully. The hand-back and unrecorded guards judge replies at turn end the same way. 0091 assumed a refused reply never took effect.
decision: (1) A guard holds a value only by checking an act before it takes effect: a dispatch, a change to the journal or the work, a tool call. Such an attempt, when refused, never took effect, and is recorded as drift held by the guard, as 0091 said. (2) A reply shown as it is written has taken effect, refused or not: a turn-end refusal does not hold it, and the reply counts as delivered when judged. (3) So the guards that judge replies at turn end (bottom-line, hand-back and unrecorded) cannot hold their values, and leave this cut now, applying 0104's split without waiting for judgment: those guards, the ordering value's realization and every example held only by them move unchanged into cut 7, which holds them by the architect's own text and checks them by examples. The guards that check acts before they take effect (the readback gate, descend, past-objective and the dispatch checks) stay. (4) The current judgment judges the cut without the moved examples.
consequences: Cut 7 gains the architect's text for ordering, hand-back in replies and recording before reporting; the moved examples keep their meaning. 0097's per-topic action reading is revisited there with the acts-before-reply timing in view.
